quote_original: And the word “perdition” means “death and destruction.”
context_before: Bear in mind, this is not secular history, but salvation history; so who is this son of perdition that is lost? Scholars claim it is one called Judas, but that is not true. If you want to get close to the answer, read the 18th Psalm, which is repeated in the 22nd chapter of 2 Samuel. This is a hymn David sings, praising the Lord for saving him from death and destruction.

quote_original: Judas is Judah, the Lion’s whelp.
context_before: The son of perdition has nothing to do with any Judas, for he is the one who betrays the messianic secret. No one could ever betray you but yourself, for no one knows your secret but yourself!
context_after: He is the only son named in the genealogy of Jesus. “Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.” Judah is the one who knows and tells the secret.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Mystery Of Life (1969-12-12).

quote_original: Then he awakes, wearing that individualized face which is perfect.
context_before: Hold to him. His name is I am. He loves his emanation and will cleave to him and they will become one.
context_after: I will meet you in eternity and I will know you; but for all the identity of person, there will be a discontinuity of form. A form that is glorious beyond the wildest dream of man. The form is all power, all wisdom, and all love. We purposely descended into this world to accomplish that end.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Mystery Of Life (1969-12-12).
